lines.text: How can a tiny square of random black and white pixels beam a website link to your camera in half a second?
Invented in nineteen ninety-four to track auto parts in Japan, QR stands for Quick Response.
Those three large squares in the corners are position markers that tell your phone camera orientation and angle.
The smaller square near the bottom right aligns the image to correct distortion.
The remaining grid of pixels encodes characters into binary ones and zeros.
Even better, QR codes feature Reed-Solomon error correction, meaning they scan perfectly even if thirty percent is ripped or dirty.
A simple two-dimensional barcode connects the physical world to the digital universe.
